blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Hotspots originate from stationary plumes of hot mantle material.
Unlike most volcanoes, hotspots produce volcanic activity independent of plate boundaries.
Continuous plate motion over a stationary hotspot generates age-progressive volcanic chains.
The Hawaiian Islands are a textbook example of a hotspot-generated volcanic island chain.
Hotspot volcanism occurs independent of plate boundaries, which is a frequent conceptual question in geology.
Remember that hotspots remain stationary while tectonic plates move over them, creating age-progressive volcano chains like the Hawaiian Islands.

blocks.content: • Plate motion over hotspots forms age-progressive volcanoes.
